subject: Error: java.lang.RuntimeException: PipeMapRed.waitOutputThreads(): subprocess failed with code 1

messages.author: c5408a10708be3e9
messages.subject: Error: java.lang.RuntimeException: PipeMapRed.waitOutputThreads(): subprocess failed with code 1
parts:
Hi,

I'm a newbie to RHadoop and Hadoop.
I created a cluster with 4 nodes using Cloudera and after that install R and rmr2 on each nodes and rhdfs on the NameNode.

I was trying a simple test with rmr2 and rhdfs:

Sys.setenv(HADOOP_HOME="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-5.3.1-1.cdh5.3.1.p0.5/lib/hadoop")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-5.3.1-1.cdh5.3.1.p0.5/bin/hadoop")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-5.3.1-1.cdh5.3.1.p0.5/lib/hadoop-0.20-mapreduce/contrib/streaming/hadoop-streaming-2.5.0-mr1-cdh5.3.1.jar")
Sys.setenv(JAVA_HOME="/usr/java/jdk1.7.0_67-cloudera")

library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)

hdfs.init()
out <- mapreduce(input = 'Geo_Datamining.csv', map = function(k, v) keyval(v, v^2))
df <- as.data.frame(from.dfs(out))

after calling mapreduce function job starts and it fails with error :

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1976] Error: java.lang.RuntimeException: PipeMapRed.waitOutputThreads(): subprocess failed with code 1
parts: First I would take a look at the debugging guide, so that you learn how to report bugs in this context. Unfortunately the console output is not very often sufficient to solve a problem. In your case, guessing from file name extensions, you are reading a CSV file without specifying the format, so I'd read about the input.format argument to mapreduce and the make.input.format function. It seems to me this would be a very difficult package to use just going by intuition. The manual is there to be read.
